Theme

Latin word

plērīque

plērīque, plēraeque, plēraque

adjective, plural (the singular plērusque is rare and post-classical)

most, most people, the greater number

In this lexicon

  • most

    the recommended word · classical · Quint. 4.2.31: plērīque scrīptōrēs; Cic. Inv. 1.65: multī nihil prōdesse philosophiam, plērīque etiam obesse arbitrantur (Lewis & Short); Traupman 347

Examples

  • plēraque sunt vocābula quibus vulgō ūtimur, neque tamen liquidō scīmus quid ea propriē atque vērē significent

    most of the words we use every day, we don’t clearly know what they properly and truly meanGell. 16.5.1

    In the entry for most

  • quod plēraque nōs illā quasi mūgiente M litterā clūdimus

    because we end most words with that letter M, which sounds almost like mooingQuint. 12.10.30

    In the entry for most

  • eam plērīque scrīptōrēs, maximē quī sunt ab Isocrate, volunt esse lūcidam, brevem, vērīsimilem

    most writers, especially those of Isocrates’ school, want it to be clear, short and believableQuint. 4.2.31

    In the entry for most

  • magna pars vītae ēlābitur male agentibus, maxima nihil agentibus, tōta vīta aliud agentibus

    a great part of life slips away while we do wrong, most of it while we do nothing, the whole of it while we do something elseSen. Ep. 1.1

    In the entry for most

    the old statues show that there were once no barbers, since most of them have long hair and a big beardVarr. RR 2.11.10

    In the entry for most

  • ēvigilō cum libuit, plērumque circā hōram prīmam, saepe ante, tardius rārō

    I wake when I please, mostly about sunrise, often before, seldom laterPlin. Ep. 9.36.1

    In the entry for most
